reference_screen.role: design ideas only; no source, dependency, runtime, or production path imported
findings: FlashInfer's inspected portable FP4 dequantization uses a floating lookup and multiplication, while native FP4 conversion paths target newer architectures; neither is an SM87 hot-path replacement.
CUTLASS's compatible E2M1-to-BF16 x4 helper uses six PRMT instructions, versus five PRMT instructions in the retained native x4 decoder.
Triton's NVIDIA E2M1-to-BF16 x8 lowering uses ten PRMT instructions, equal to two retained native x4 decoders; it does not reduce the SM87 decode work.
The bounded native experiment therefore targeted the adjacent shared-scale load stream rather than replacing the retained exact decoder with a heavier reference lowering.

candidate.shape: exact-C512 NVFP4 Gate/Up M128xN256xK64, 272 CTAs per branch, 256 threads
retained_components: canonical packed NVFP4 weights and canonical E4M3 scales
compact 32-byte B shared rows with retained half swizzle
exact table-free E2M1 decoder and shared E4M3-to-BF16 codebook
zero persistent sidecar and zero workspace

change.baseline: for each of four K16 phases, load one encoded E4M3 U8 from each of four output panels
change.candidate: before the K16 loop, load one aligned U32 containing all four consecutive E4M3 codes from each output panel; select each later byte in registers
change.intended_effect: replace sixteen scalar shared loads per stage body with four vector shared loads and reduce shared LSU pressure
change.compiled_effect: four LDS.U32 plus twelve nonzero-byte SHF extractions replace sixteen LDS.U8; the load wavefront count falls, but total hot-loop work does not

environment.device: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin Developer Kit

real_generation_direction.prompt: P513; 501 space-separated copies of hello in the pinned non-thinking chat template

matched_ncu.payload: pinned real Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 layer-0 Gate weight and scale tensors with deterministic BF16 activation
interpretation: The candidate achieves the narrow LSU goal: ordinary shared-load wavefronts fall exactly 6.25%, while compact async landing, global sectors, excessive wavefronts, and bank conflicts do not change.

The compiler replaces the twelve avoided non-low-byte U8 loads with twelve SHF extractions. Four additional live scale words raise registers from 241 to 245, and executed instructions rise 0.464% instead of falling.

Grouping the four scale loads before the K16 consumers also lengthens their live range and creates a burst dependency. MIO-throttle and barrier samples rise, tensor utilization falls slightly, and the real Gate launch regresses 0.242%.

A scale-load successor is eligible only if it removes total work, for example through a changed producer representation or fused conversion; another load-hoist/extract permutation on the canonical byte layout is excluded.

decision.reason: The real P513 generation path regresses Prefix by 1.090 ms and TTFT by 0.912 ms. Matched NCU confirms that 6.25% fewer shared-load wavefronts are offset by 0.464% more instructions, four more registers, and a 0.242% Gate regression.
decision.retained_route: the exact-C512 M128xN256 production kernel with scalar encoded-scale loads
decision.stop_loss: Do not build a complete B-C-C-B harness, run NSys, or screen more extraction permutations after the real path is non-positive and matched NCU shows no total-work reduction.
decision.reopen_when: Only a producer/layout change that removes both the scalar loads and compensating byte extraction, while retaining real-checkpoint correctness and bounded ownership, may reopen scale feed work.

limitations: The performance direction is one fresh fixed-clock baseline/candidate process pair, sufficient to reject a non-positive direction but not a latency distribution.
The NCU comparison covers one pinned real layer-0 Gate launch with deterministic BF16 activation; it is causal diagnostic evidence, not whole-model throughput authority.
The candidate source was intentionally reverted and its binaries are retained only under /tmp with hashes; no experimental production path remains in the repository.
No multi-request, serving, power, energy, or scheduler-overlap claim is made.
